binders: K and ρ are the constant material parameters, respectively bulk modulus of compressibility and density; the passage introduces them descriptively rather than with an explicit universal quantifier [printed p. 2, paragraph after (1.5)].
A is the 2 × 2 real matrix [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]] [printed p. 2, (1.6); printed p. 1, real-matrix convention after (1.1)].
c is defined by c = √(K/ρ) [printed p. 2, immediately after w¹ = p + ρcu].
hypotheses: A is specifically the constant-coefficient acoustics matrix of (1.6) for the one-dimensional material described by K and ρ [printed p. 2, (1.5)–(1.6); printed p. 3, selected sentence].

The source uses a real sound speed and the coefficient 1/ρ; ordinary real interpretation therefore requires a defined reciprocal and real square root. These domain requirements are inferred from the displayed expressions, not stated as explicit inequalities in the selected passage [printed p. 2, (1.6) and c = √(K/ρ)].
conclusions: The acoustics matrix A has eigenvalues −c and +c, where c = √(K/ρ) [printed p. 3, opening paragraph, selected sentence; printed p. 2, definition of c].

These signed eigenvalues give the acoustic wave propagation speeds in the one-dimensional medium [printed p. 3, selected sentence]; +c corresponds to rightward propagation and −c to leftward propagation [printed p. 2, equations for w¹ and w² and accompanying explanation].
definitions_and_conventions: The state order is q = [p, u]ᵀ, so A has upper-right entry K and lower-left entry 1/ρ [printed p. 2, (1.6)].
p denotes pressure, more precisely its perturbation from a constant background pressure, and u denotes particle velocity [printed p. 2, paragraph after (1.5)].
K denotes bulk modulus of compressibility, and ρ denotes density; both are constants describing the material [printed p. 2, paragraph after (1.5)].

c = √(K/ρ) denotes the speed of sound; the square-root notation supplies the nonnegative root under its ordinary real interpretation [printed p. 2, definition of c and ensuing identification as sound speed].
The scalar fields w¹ = p + ρcu and w² = p − ρcu satisfy transport equations with coefficients c and −c, respectively [printed p. 2, discussion following (1.6)].
implicit_context: The enclosing framework is a homogeneous first-order system q_t + A q_x = 0 with constant real coefficients [printed p. 1, (1.1) and following paragraph].
The acoustic example models waves in both directions along a one-dimensional medium [printed p. 2, introduction to (1.5)].
The preceding discussion relates a complete family of real eigenvectors to decomposition into waves and identifies eigenvalues with propagation speeds [printed p. 3, opening paragraph].

Positive sound speed is part of the preceding physical discussion of a wave traveling to the right with c > 0; the selected matrix sentence does not independently state positivity assumptions on K or ρ [printed p. 2, introduction to (1.4), and paragraph after (1.5); printed p. 3, selected sentence].

details: The spectral claim concerns [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]], with the parameter placement fixed by (1.6) [printed p. 2, (1.6)].
Both signs are part of the claim: −√(K/ρ) and +√(K/ρ) [printed p. 3, selected sentence; printed p. 2, definition of c].

The source presents these as the two eigenvalues of the two-component acoustics matrix; it does not separately formulate a characteristic-polynomial identity or a theorem about algebraic multiplicities [printed p. 2, (1.6); printed p. 3, selected sentence].
The eigenvalues are signed wave speeds, while c itself is the sound speed [printed p. 3, selected sentence; printed p. 2, discussion of w¹ and w²].
The two characteristic scalar equations describe opposite directions of acoustic propagation [printed p. 2, equations for w¹ and w²; printed p. 3, opening sentence].
The selected assertion identifies eigenvalues and their wave-speed interpretation; explicit eigenvectors are not supplied in that sentence [printed p. 3, selected sentence].
The general definition of hyperbolicity supplies surrounding motivation but is distinct from the specific eigenvalue identification [printed p. 3, opening paragraph].

undebatable_constraints: Preserve A = [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]] and the state order [p, u]ᵀ [printed p. 2, (1.6)].
Preserve c = √(K/ρ), including the order of the quotient [printed p. 2, definition following w¹].
Preserve both eigenvalues −c and +c [printed p. 3, selected sentence].
Preserve the interpretation of these eigenvalues as the acoustic propagation speeds in the one-dimensional medium [printed p. 3, selected sentence].
Do not attribute explicitly stated inequalities K > 0 or ρ > 0 to this passage: its parameter paragraph supplies physical roles but no such inequalities [printed p. 2, paragraph after (1.5)].

ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must make its domain precise. Positivity assumptions may express the intended physical setting, but must be distinguished from explicit source hypotheses; unrestricted arbitrary real parameters are not supported.

ambiguities.issue: Degenerate cases and eigenvalue multiplicities are not discussed.
ambiguities.evidence: Printed p. 3 describes two distinct acoustic waves and lists eigenvalues −c and +c; printed p. 2 identifies c as sound speed, without a separate treatment of c = 0.
ambiguities.impact: The passage does not settle a formal extension to zero sound speed, repeated eigenvalues, or the associated failure of an independent eigenvector decomposition.

contract_plain_english: For the constant real acoustics matrix A = [[0, K], [1/ρ, 0]], where K is the material's bulk modulus and ρ its density, define c = √(K/ρ) as the sound speed [printed p. 2, (1.6) and following discussion]. The selected source sentence states that A has eigenvalues −c and +c and that these are the acoustic propagation speeds in the one-dimensional medium [printed p. 3, opening paragraph]. The preceding characteristic equations identify +c with rightward travel and −c with leftward travel [printed p. 2, discussion of w¹ and w²]. The physical parameter domain is implicit; explicit positivity inequalities and degenerate cases are not supplied in this passage [printed p. 2, material-parameter paragraph and sound-speed discussion].
